prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: The `crit^2` soft gate in the locality term over-suppresses moderate-criticality neighbours and lets the cut term dominate on C1 (cut 137→148, crit_cross 0.011→0.016); replacing the squared gate with a linear gate `crit` widens the pool of pulled-together critical pairs by roughly a factor of the mean crit, moving well over 1-2% of nodes and directly attacking the strongest-paying statistic (crit_cross, rho=-0.65) without touching any coefficient granularity that previously produced duplicates.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=+0.127 robust(mean-std)=-0.004 min_case=-0.005 seed_std=0.038 tns_mean=+0.031 all_valid=True
  C1: score=+0.105 dWNS=+14.7% dTNS=+8.4% per-seed=[+0.06 +0.07 +0.18]
  C2: score=+0.028 dWNS=+5.6% dTNS=+1.3% per-seed=[+0.08 +0.00 +0.00]
  C3: score=-0.005 dWNS=-2.1% dTNS=+0.5% per-seed=[-0.02 -0.03 +0.03]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->142, wcut 421->418, crit_cross 0.011->0.016, repair_flips 103->120, changed-vs-baseline 16.3%
  C2: cut 318->305, wcut 1007->962, crit_cross 0.000->0.000, repair_flips 238->238, changed-vs-baseline 6.2%
  C3: cut 582->587, wcut 1955->1968, crit_cross 0.069->0.062, repair_flips 353->350, changed-vs-baseline 3.6%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response:
(1) Partly. Linear gate widened critical-pair pull as predicted (C1 crit_cross 0.011→0.016, changed 16.3%), but cut rose 137→142 and repair_flips 103→120, so the cut term still dominates—hypothesis's "over-suppression" claim not cleanly confirmed.

(2) C1 drove gains (dWNS +14.7%, dTNS +8.4%) via more critical pairs co-located, but at cost of extra cut nets and repair flips. C2 improved cut/wcut with flat crit_cross. C3 slightly regressed (dWNS -2.1%).

(3) Seed spread 0.038 with min_case -0.005 and robust -0.004—marginal, C3 per-seed straddles zero; not comfortably acceptable.

(4) Next: add a mild cut penalty or cap changed-vs-baseline on C1 to curb repair_flips, then re-test seed stability on C3.
